findings.description: setClaimEnabled(false) is the deployed default and closes claim:440 as the reward path, leaving autoAnnihilate:516 as the only user-facing mint. autoAnnihilate carries two liveness dependencies claim does not: (a) it requires poolState == Active (:517), and (b) its annihilatable leg calls antimatter.annihilate (:601), which is whenNotPaused against ANTIMATTER'S OWN Phoenix pauser (lib/antimatter@a5570ce Antimatter.sol:255) - a pauser StableStaker does not control. Consequences a non-malicious owner would plausibly be surprised by: with claimEnabled == false, (1) a pool moved to Migrating has NO open reward path at all (claim reverts on the gate, autoAnnihilate reverts on :517) until the migration exit runs; (2) a pause of the foreign Antimatter contract locks every caller with netWanted > 0 out of their accrued reward, with the only remedy being an owner setClaimEnabled(true) on a possibly-unavailable owner key.
evidence: src/StableStakerV2.sol:279  function setClaimEnabled(bool enabled) external onlyOwner
src/StableStakerV2.sol:517  require(poolState[token] == PoolState.Active, "StableStaker: pool not active");
missingMitigations: No auto-reopen of claim when poolState leaves Active
No local check that antimatter is unpaused before steering the only reward path through it

findings.genuineOrShapeMatch: genuine, but the pattern maps only loosely (CENTRALIZATION-ADMIN is a generic single-key template); the real content is the cross-contract liveness coupling, not key custody.

findings.description: claimEnabled is read at exactly one site (:440) and therefore gates claim ONLY. autoAnnihilate:605 mints RAW Antimatter to msg.sender's wallet with no claimEnabled check. For a caller with user.amount == 0 and a non-zero unclaimedReward backlog the arithmetic collapses to principalAsAntimatter = 0 -> capped = 0 -> netWanted = 0 -> excessBase = owed, so the ENTIRE backlog is minted raw at :605: autoAnnihilate is a complete functional substitute for the disabled claim. The same path also widens whenever gross is capped below what netWanted needs, since excess = excessBase + (netWanted - netUsed) * scale (:596).
evidence: src/StableStakerV2.sol:542  uint256 capped = owed < principalAsAntimatter ? owed : principalAsAntimatter;
src/StableStakerV2.sol:596  uint256 excess = excessBase + (netWanted - netUsed) * scale;
missingMitigations: No claimEnabled (or equivalent policy) gate on the raw-AM excess mint
findings.genuineOrShapeMatch: The GATE BYPASS is genuine and mechanically verified. The PATTERN'S OWN HARM (over-mint) does NOT apply and must not be claimed: autoAnnihilate re-uses byte-identical settle arithmetic to claim (:538-539 vs :442-446), drains unclaimedReward, and re-bases rewardDebt, so the header emission cap is intact. Conservation checks out exactly: minted = annihilatable + excess = owed - (capped - netWanted*scale), with the sub-unit remainder carried at :548. Impact is therefore spec/policy deviation, not value creation - Low unless story-025 states the teaching-phase gate is absolute, which is a Law-2 question for story-faithfulness, not for this tier.
findings.suppressionNote: The in-source NatSpec at :471-474 calls this 'a knowing, documented loophole'. Per the standing rule that in-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority, that comment does not sanitize the finding; only story-025 or owner triage can.

manualReview.type: linear pro-ration of a non-linear floor
manualReview.description: netFloor = (netQuote * gross) / grossQuote linearly rescales a floor that the market strategy computes non-linearly (_exitFloor = convertToAssets(convertToShares(gross)) * (MAX_BPS - slip) / MAX_BPS, ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:127-135). The division floors, which LOOSENS the safety check.
evidence: src/StableStakerV2.sol:558  gross = grossQuote > user.amount ? user.amount : grossQuote;
src/StableStakerV2.sol:587  uint256 allowance = EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE + (netFloor * EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE_BPS) / MAX_BPS;
manualReview.assessment: SHAPE MATCH, most likely not a finding. This is NOT the Linear-Depletion class the family was bitten by: there the linear formula was applied to a compounding/decaying quantity so the error accumulated as a RATE DRIFT. Here _exitFloor is linear in gross up to two floor() operations, so the pro-ration error is O(1) raw units and does not scale with gross. It is bounded by the 2-unit flat allowance below 10_000 raw units of netFloor and by the 1 bp proportional leg above it (1 bp >> a few raw units at any realistic size). No leak either: the direction of the error only slackens an anti-bypass check, it cannot mis-pay. Kept in manual review rather than dropped because the claim 'two floors cost at most 2 units' is asserted from the source, not proven; a Tier-3 bound would close it.

manualReview.patternFitNote: weak/adjacent - the DB has no preview-vs-actual pattern; this is the inverse of the DB's 'step 2 re-reads a live value' shape (here step 1 probes a DIFFERENT argument than step 2 uses).
manualReview.description: The availability gate probes previewExitFor(token, address(this), 1) and only asserts grossQuote > 0 for a ONE-UNIT request; the real call at :556 previews the caller's full netWanted. A strategy (or a live vault/AMM state) that answers positively for 1 unit can return a deeply CAPPED quote for the real amount - grossToRequest capped to clientBalances, or sharesToSell capped to held shares (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:162-187). :557 only catches grossQuote == 0.
manualReview.assessment: The divergence is REAL and mechanically confirmed. Its harm is not a loss - a capped quote shrinks gross, the caller is debited less principal, and the displaced reward is minted raw at :605 - i.e. it FEEDS PATTERN-002 rather than causing an independent leak. The availability view's stated purpose (refusing to hand the caller a bypass of a closed claim, NatSpec :1044-1048) is therefore only enforced at the 1-unit granularity it probes. Low, and adjudication belongs to the interaction tier.

manualReview.type: par-exit on the shared underwater buffer, reached from a NEW entry point
manualReview.description: autoAnnihilate passes guardUnderwater = true (:579), but that branch does not revert when the idle buffer covers the request: it emits BufferWithdrawn, calls strategy.relinquishPrincipal(token, gross) and returns gross VERBATIM (:1186-1195). With a market strategy gross = ceilDiv(netWanted * MAX_BPS, MAX_BPS - slip) > netWanted, so received == gross, the floor check passes trivially, netUsed = netWanted, and surplus = gross - netWanted is transferred back to the caller at :609. The caller exits at PAR while the strategy is below par - the same allocation-rule arbitrage as the prior entries - via a path that consumes the grossed-up figure of the shared buffer per unit of reward annihilated.

The underwater buffer pays daily-volume withdrawals at par during transient, mean-reverting underwater dips to avoid sparking panic and to avoid forcing users to realise losses by redeeming shares at the bottom; bank-run / mass-exit is handled separately by migrateOut with pro-rata distribution.

manualReview.reFileBasis: DISCLOSED, NOT RE-FILED. A new fingerprint would mint if this were filed on autoAnnihilate rather than _routeExit, and dedup would not catch it - hence the explicit disclosure. But the re-file basis is weak and this tier does not assert one: (a) the per-caller bite is still capped by their own principal (gross = min(grossQuote, user.amount), :558), so no larger buffer drain than withdraw already permits; (b) autoAnnihilate is whenNotPaused, so the operational pause() mitigation the owner named for 2b9a89d29c covers it unchanged; (c) the caller is value-neutral against their own books (they surrender gross and receive netWanted of phUSD plus surplus of token). The one genuinely new observation is the RATE: autoAnnihilate consumes the grossed-up gross of buffer per unit of reward, where withdraw requests exactly amount - relevant to the owner's 'daily-volume' sizing assumption, and the reason this is surfaced rather than dropped.

manualReview.description: Every other token movement in the new code is balance-measured (_routeExit:1196-1198, _pullToken:1109), but the annihilation leg mints annihilatable = netUsed * scale of Antimatter (:598-599) and then lets Antimatter PULL netUsed through the forceApprove at :600. On a fee-on-transfer token Antimatter receives less than netUsed while burning AM sized for the full netUsed, under-backing the annihilation on the foreign contract's side.
manualReview.assessment: Almost certainly C4-invalid: the token set is an owner-curated stablecoin allowlist (addToken:252) that must ALSO be registered on the phUSD stable minter, and generic fee-on-transfer is known-invalid unless in scope. Recorded rather than dropped only because the harm would land on the FOREIGN Antimatter/phUSD contract's backing, not on StableStaker, so it would not be caught by this contract's own conservation checks.

checkedNoMatch.result: NO MATCH on the over-mint leg (the gate-bypass leg is PATTERN-002)
checkedNoMatch.evidence: Conservation verified by hand: annihilatable + excess = netUsed*scale + excessBase + (netWanted-netUsed)*scale = owed - (capped - netWanted*scale), the remainder being carried at :548. Single _updatePool writer; unclaimedReward drained, not incremented.

The netWanted == 0 escape at :557 was checked for a zero-net-but-nonzero-gross principal debit. It cannot occur: netWanted == 0 requires capped < scale; if user.amount >= 1 then principalAsAntimatter >= scale so capped = owed < scale, making excessBase = owed - capped = 0 and the require at :546 revert. Hence netWanted == 0 implies user.amount == 0, and gross = min(grossQuote, 0) = 0. The saturating floorWithAllowance at :588 is likewise safe (it only collapses when netFloor <= 2 raw units).

minPhUSDOut is a caller parameter forwarded verbatim to antimatter.annihilate (:601) for the phUSD leg; the token-exit leg is bounded by the measured received >= floorWithAllowance check at :589 plus the market strategy's own byte-identical minOut in _disposeShares.
